title: The Evening Brief: Two Indonesia quakes, Hawaii hurricane warning, two campus shootings
dek: Saturday closes with disasters still unresolved rather than settled: Indonesia's earthquake toll near 47, a hurricane warning holding for Hawaii's Big Island, and active investigations into shootings in Michigan and at Virginia State University.
author: GoCheckMyNews
key_fact: Multiple emergencies remained open at day's end, with final tolls, storm tracks, and shooting motives all still pending official confirmation.
bottom_line: Saturday's reporting centered on emergencies still in progress: two Indonesia earthquakes with a rising death toll, a hurricane warning holding for Hawaii's Big Island, and unsolved shootings in Michigan and at Virginia State University that left investigators without a disclosed motive. A federal judge's decision to lift the stay on Somalia's TPS termination, citing a Supreme Court ruling that narrowed judicial review, marked the day's most significant legal development, alongside a new Justice Department opinion expanding military arrest authority near the border. The reporting documents each event's numbers and mechanics but does not resolve final tolls, storm tracks, or the motives behind the shootings. Checkpoints ahead include updated hurricane advisories, Indonesia's casualty counts as rescue teams reach isolated areas, and any arrests or motive disclosures in the two shootings.
body: Saturday's news cycle was defined by events still unfolding rather than concluded. Two earthquakes struck eastern Indonesia within hours of each other, a hurricane warning stayed in effect for Hawaii's Big Island as Tropical Storm Lala approached, and two separate mass shootings in Michigan and at Virginia State University remained under active investigation with no motives disclosed. Layered onto this were a federal court ruling narrowing legal protections for Somali nationals and a new Justice Department opinion expanding military authority near the border.

In Indonesia, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit the Flores region at 5:58 a.m. local time, followed hours later by a 6.4-magnitude quake on Sumatra. Reporting through the day put the death toll at least at 47, with 50 hospitalized and about 2,000 villagers displaced. Earlier figures in the day's reporting cited a toll of 38 before later dispatches raised it to 47; landslides cut off the Trans-Flores Highway and power outages disabled communications, complicating rescue efforts across six regencies. More than 235 aftershocks were recorded, the largest at magnitude 6.2.

In Hawaii, the National Hurricane Center kept a hurricane warning in effect for the Big Island as Tropical Storm Lala approached, with sustained winds near 65 mph as of Friday evening and forecasts of up to 25 inches of rain and a 3-foot storm surge. Gov. Josh Green declared a state of emergency. On Molokai, the National Weather Service Honolulu issued a Tropical Storm Warning with peak winds of 35-45 mph and gusts to 55 mph forecast for Saturday afternoon into early Sunday. Hawaii's last hurricane landfall was Hurricane Iniki in 1992.

Two shootings compounded the day's violence. In rural Missaukee County, Michigan, five people were killed Friday across multiple locations; a 13-year-old girl, shot four times, called 911 and was the sole survivor, later listed in stable condition. The suspect, 39-year-old Chad Hickman, was found dead near one of the victims. Authorities have disclosed no motive. At Virginia State University in Ettrick, Virginia, five people were shot outside a residence hall around 1:28 a.m. Saturday; one victim remains in critical condition, and multiple suspects remained at large as of the day's reporting, with no arrests announced.

Separately, U.S. District Judge Allison Burroughs in Boston lifted a stay blocking the Trump administration's termination of Temporary Protected Status for Somali nationals, citing a June Supreme Court ruling in Mullin v. Doe that limited judicial review of TPS decisions. Burroughs acknowledged plaintiffs had presented a compelling case and faced irreparable harm but said the high court's ruling constrained her authority. Reporting put the number of Somali nationals currently holding TPS at 2,471, with another 1,383 applications pending. Also Friday, the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel, in an opinion authored by Deputy Assistant Attorney General William Hyde, concluded that military personnel can arrest migrants for trespassing near and outside designated National Defense Areas on the southern border without violating the Posse Comitatus Act.

The reporting does not say what caused either shooting, nor does it resolve Lala's final landfall track or Indonesia's ultimate death toll. On the Somalia TPS ruling, the reporting is clear on the legal mechanism, the Supreme Court precedent constraining the judge, and the numbers affected, but does not say whether plaintiffs will pursue further appeals or whether Fifth Amendment discrimination claims will proceed separately.

Desk boards were unavailable this cycle, so figures in this edition reflect the day's published reporting rather than a current official record; readers should treat tolls and storm parameters as of each story's stated reporting time.

What to watch in the coming days: updated National Hurricane Center advisories on Lala's track and Big Island impacts through Saturday and Sunday; Indonesia's National Disaster Management Agency casualty updates as rescue teams reach villages cut off by landslides; identification of suspects and any arrests in the Virginia State University shooting; disclosure of a motive and completed victim identifications in the Michigan case; and whether Somalia TPS plaintiffs file further appeals or whether DHS sets a formal termination date.
